newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai brokers asked to avoid spreading rumours.
newsitem.headline: Thai brokers asked to avoid spreading rumours.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) had asked all 50 member brokers to avoid spreading rumours which could cause turmoil on the stock market, a SET board member told reporters on Wednesday.
"The SET on Tuesday asked all brokerage firms to cooperate and stop spreading rumours," SET board member Pakhawat Kovithvathanphong told reporters.
Pakhawat, who is also the president of major Thai brokerage Securities One Plc, said the bourse's move would be aimed at preventing unfounded rumours from affecting the stock market in the future.
He did not say if any penalty would be imposed on any broker found spreading rumours.
The stock market last Friday was hit hard by unfounded rumours that some finance companies had financial problems due to client defaults on margin loans.
The Bank of Thailand, the SET and several finance firms denied the rumours, but the SET index tumbled near to three-year lows on widespread selling.
